blogs.title: When HIT Hits Early: Pre‑op Cath Heparin and the POD1–4 Platelet Crash
blogs.description: Early postoperative thrombocytopenia is usually blamed on CPB, but recent preoperative heparin (even a small cath lab dose) can prime classic or autoimmune HIT to present before POD5. This post reviews timing pitfalls, how to adapt the 4Ts in cardiac surgery, and the key historical questions that prevent a missed diagnosis.

blogs.title: Autoimmune HIT 101: Heparin‑Independent Platelet Activation After Cardiac Surgery
blogs.description: Autoimmune HIT can follow cardiac surgery and is marked by profound thrombocytopenia, arterial thrombosis risk, and SRA activation at 0 U/mL heparin. We’ll cover how aHIT differs from classic HIT, why it’s more prothrombotic, and the clinical cues that should push you toward urgent non‑heparin therapy.

blogs.title: The SRA Isn’t Binary: Making Sense of Atypical Results and FcγR Blockade Resistance
blogs.description: An ‘indeterminate’ SRA with strong activation at low heparin, activation at 0 U/mL, and only partial inhibition with IV.3 can still equal aHIT. Learn how to interpret raw SRA data, when to request additional testing (PF4‑enhanced assays, P‑selectin expression), and how to integrate lab nuance with bedside decision‑making.

blogs.title: Argatroban vs Fondaparinux in HIT: Choosing, Switching, and Why Antithrombin May Matter
blogs.description: Direct thrombin inhibitors offer short half‑life control after stroke, while fondaparinux is convenient and effective off‑label—especially if hypercoagulability persists. We’ll discuss selection in renal/hepatic dysfunction, bedside signals to switch, monitoring strategies, and the rationale for giving antithrombin with fondaparinux when AT is low.

blogs.title: IVIG for Autoimmune HIT: Expectations, Dosing, and What to Do When It Underwhelms
blogs.description: High‑dose IVIG can rapidly reverse thrombocytopenia in aHIT by blocking Fc‑mediated platelet activation—but not always. This post outlines dosing (1–2 g/kg), timing, safety, predictors of response, and contingency plans when platelets lag despite therapy.

blogs.title: Reading the Tea Leaves: Using Fibrinogen, D‑dimer, and Schistocytes to Track HIT Control
blogs.description: Falling fibrinogen, rising D‑dimer, and new schistocytes can flag ongoing HIT‑driven consumptive coagulopathy even after you’ve started the ‘right’ drug. Here’s a practical approach to serial labs as a bedside barometer of anticoagulant efficacy and when to escalate or switch therapy.

blogs.title: Stroke in HIT: Beyond DVT—Recognizing and Treating Arterial Events
blogs.description: Arterial thrombosis—including cortical infarcts—occurs in HIT and can masquerade as postoperative delirium. We’ll cover thresholds for neuroimaging, balancing hemorrhagic risk in the immediate post‑stroke window, and anticoagulant selection when platelets are critically low.

blogs.title: Post‑Cardiac Surgery Thrombocytopenia: Don’t Miss HIT Among the Usual Suspects
blogs.description: Differentiate CPB‑related nadirs, infection, DIC, drug‑induced thrombocytopenia, PTP, and TTP from HIT. This guide emphasizes timing, the depth of the platelet fall, associated coagulopathy, the impact of LMWH prophylaxis, and how a pre‑op cath exposure can flip your pretest probability.

blogs.title: Antibody Evolution in HIT: From Autoimmune to Heparin‑Dependent and the Implications
blogs.description: HIT serologies can evolve over weeks—from heparin‑independent activation to classic heparin‑dependent patterns. Learn what persistent SRA positivity means, how it informs duration of non‑heparin anticoagulation, and cautious strategies around future heparin exposure.

blogs.title: A Practical ICU Pathway for Suspected aHIT
blogs.description: A stepwise bedside algorithm: stop all heparins, start a non‑heparin anticoagulant, send PF4 ELISA plus a functional assay, consider IVIG for aHIT, screen for silent thromboses, and use fibrinogen/D‑dimer to judge control. Includes tips for transitions (DTI to fondaparinux to DOAC) and consult triggers.
